Q: Why does BLE-program ble_simple_central.py respond with <memoryview> instead of data A:

It is perfectly normal for MicroPython’s Bluetooth stack to return a memoryview object. This isn't an error; it is an intentional design choice for efficiency.

In MicroPython, a memoryview is a way to access the internal data of an object (like a buffer) without making a copy of it. Since the Raspberry Pi Pico W has limited RAM, MicroPython uses memoryview to handle incoming BLE packets quickly without wasting memory on repetitive string or byte conversions.
More details here::
https://docs.micropython.org/en/latest/library/bluetooth.html
From the section titled Event Handling on that page:

"Note: As an optimisation to prevent unnecessary allocations, the addr, adv_data, char_data, notify_data, and uuid entries in the tuples are read-only memoryview instances pointing to bluetooth’s internal ringbuffer, and are only valid during the invocation of the IRQ handler function."

Why you see <memoryview>

When you run print("RX", v), Python looks at the type of v. Because v is a memoryview, it showd <memoryview>. It DOES NOT automatically "peek" inside and show you the bytes unless you tell it to.

How to fix it

To see the actual data, you need to convert the memoryview into a format that print() understands as data—usually bytes or a str.

Option 1: Convert to Bytes

If you just want to see the hex or raw data:

Python

def on_rx(v):
 
    print("RX", bytes(v))

Option 2: Convert to String

If you know the peripheral is sending text (like the "0_" strings in the demo):

Python

def on_rx(v):
    # Convert to bytes, then decode to a string
    print("RX", bytes(v).decode('utf-8'))

Q: Learning MERN in 2026 is it relly worth it? A:

Honestly, I'd recommend starting with the MERN stack and then picking up some cloud skills along the way. AI/ML sounds exciting, but it has a steep learning curve with all the math involved, and most entry-level ML roles want experience or advanced degrees anyway. MERN is your fastest path to actually landing internships because almost every startup needs web developers, and you can build real portfolio projects in just a few months to show off.

Hope that helps!!

Q: Unselected UITabBar item's icon color does not change in iOS26 A:

It looks like the issue is simulator-related. I have tested on the iOS 26.2 (23C55) iPhone 12 mini device and the appearance was working fine. Though, on the simulator for the same model, the appearance for the unselected items was not applied (23C54). Alternatively, it was fixed on the 23C55 but not on the 23C54 build.

Q: Why is my server socket getting two of the same message when there are two different messages being sent? A:

The problem was either in the for conn in connections: statement overwriting the conn variable and always being set to the last connection, or the fact that I was possibly overwriting the same local variables. Nevertheless, here is the answer that I got working.

def handle_client(self, conn, addr):
        print(f"Connected to {addr}")
        self.thread_count += 1
        try:
            while True:
                if conn == self.connections[0]:  ## If the connection is client 1
                    d1_data = conn.recv(1024)
                    self.data_1 = d1_data.decode()
                    console.log(f"Received {self.data_1} from {addr}","LOG")
                    if self.data_2 != "":        ## Making sure that data_2 has data
                        d2_encoded = self.data_2.encode()
                        conn.sendall(d2_encoded)
                        self.data_2 = ""
                    else:                        ## If not, let the client know
                        conn.sendall(b"lag")     ## and continue the loop
                        console.log(f"{addr} is a packet behind.", "ERROR")

This is the first half of the handle_client function used by worker threads from the threading module. Each thread handles a client. This half is used for communication with client 1.

First, it checks to make sure it is client 1. Then, it receives the data and decodes it using .decode(). Then, it makes sure the second half of the function (not pictured but it's the exact same except swapped for client 2 has data for it to send to client 1. It sends the position data from client 2 to client one.

However, if it doesn't get a packet (usually due to some sort of lag) it will let the server know and continue the loop without any hiccup. Here is the client 1 code:

def send_data():
    try:
        encoded_data = (f"{player.x_scroll}:{player.y_scroll}").encode()
        print(f"Sending {encoded_data}")
        player.sock.sendall(encoded_data)
        data = player.sock.recv(1024)
        decoded_data = data.decode()
        if decoded_data == "lag":
            return
        # parse the data
        data_list = decoded_data.split(":")
        print(data_list)
        
        ## Game-related variables
        p2.x = -int(data_list[0])+WIDTH/2-player.w/2
        p2.y = -int(data_list[1])+HEIGHT/2-player.h/2
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("aye aye")
        player.sock.close()
        quit()

Notice the lag handler just uses return to continue the send() and recv() cycle without leaving the server to hang in a comatose state.

Thank you to @Barmar and the rest of the comments for the help!

Q: can an Azure Function v4 with a 'Flex Consumption' plan have a Custom Domain? A:

Turns out the Custom Domains in AzFn Isolated v4 Flex Consumption are not restricted and you can use the Azure Portal to link a Custom Domain:

  1. Azure Portal AzFn 'Custom Domains' Click Add

  2. Choose a FQDM. e.g. subdomain.domain.dev

  3. You will be prompted to add A and TXT records to your DNS

    1. A: @ means: add an A record for {{subomain}} on your DNS with the indicated value

    2. asuid: means add a TXT record for asuid.subdomain.domain.dev with the indicated value

  4. Validate (may take anytime between TTL and 48 hours)

  5. After validation, I already has a certificate stored in my KeyVault

  6. I added Managed Identity to AzFn

  7. in KeyVault, added a policy to allow the AzFn to read certs and secrets

  8. back in AzFn custom domains, 'add/update bindings', i chose the keyvault, and then the certificate

  9. open a browser to https://subdomain.domain.dev should show

  10. if not, might need to add a CNAME: subdomain, value: {{the azfn default domain}}
